title: IEA: India to lead global oil demand growth at 3% through 2035 - The HinduBusinessLine
text:
India is expected to add 1.3 million barrels per day to oil demand by 2035, the strongest increase among emerging economies, the IEA said. | Photo Credit: iStockphoto

Global oil demand is expected to reach 106 million barrels per day (mb/d) over the next 10 years, with the strongest growth in India at 3 per cent per annum through 2035.

The International Energy Agency’s (IEA) world oil outlook anticipates that “Demand increases across nearly all sectors in emerging market and developing economies, with the strongest growth in India (3 per cent per year on average to 2035), followed by Africa (2.8 per cent) and Southeast Asia (1.4 per cent).”

Oil remains the single largest energy source through to 2050, as structural declines in demand in China and advanced economies are more than offset by growth in India, Africa and Southeast Asia, and by rising demand for international aviation. The oil price surpasses $100 per barrel in real terms by 2050, it added.

India leads oil demand growth in the Stated Policies Scenario (STEPS), adding 1.3 mb/d to 2035, which is around half of the total increase in emerging market and developing economies.

Global oil demand was 102 mb/d in 2025 and is expected to contract in 2026 due to the energy crisis caused by the conflict in the Middle East. In the CPS, it rises to 106 mb/d in 2035 and 114 mb/d in 2050, the IEA said.

The 0.4 mb/d average annual increase to 2035 is primarily driven by growth in petrochemical feedstocks (0.3 mb/d) and aviation (0.2 mb/d), while demand in most other sectors remains broadly flat or declines.

Average annual oil demand growth then picks up slightly to 0.5 mb/d through to 2050, driven mainly by the expansion of the car fleet in emerging market and developing economies outside China, where stringent fuel economy policies are not yet in place, and EV charging infrastructure remains limited.

Oil demand in advanced economies declines by an average of 0.7 per cent per year to 2035. The European Union sees the steepest decline as EV adoption accelerates fuel substitution in road transport. However, this decline is partly offset by growth in the United States, where rising petrochemical feedstock requirements and continued growth in mobility demand support higher oil consumption.

The IEA pointed out that India’s energy needs across sectors have been growing fast and are on course to continue expanding rapidly.

“In all our scenarios, India accounts for more growth in energy demand over the next decade than any other country or region in the world. The country is set to add over 12,000 cars to its roads every day over the next decade and to see a 33 per cent rise in built spaces, an additional 200 million air conditioners installed in its homes, and a surge in the production of iron, steel and cement. As a result, energy demand grows by 2.5 per cent annually to 2035 in the STEPS, triple the global rate,” it added.

India and Southeast Asia see the largest overall increase in energy needs, followed by Latin America, the Middle East and Africa. Electricity demand in India increases by an average of 6 per cent each year until 2035.
